title.en: An extended metaphor in a personal essay
title.es: Metáfora extendida en un ensayo personal

es: Sostener una metáfora extendida en un texto corto sin mezclar imágenes: abrir con la metáfora, desarrollarla con elementos del mismo campo y cerrar con una reflexión.

teaching.en: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is a step.
teaching.es: Aprender inglés es un viaje largo y cada clase es un paso.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora extendida: abres con la imagen (journey) y la sigues con step.
segments: Learning English is a long journey,
and every lesson is a step.
teaching.audioText: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is a step.

teaching.en: Grammar is my map, and vocabulary is my compass.
teaching.es: La gramática es mi mapa y el vocabulario es mi brújula.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada parte del aprendizaje recibe un elemento del viaje: así la imagen se sostiene.
teaching.audioText: Grammar is my map, and vocabulary is my compass.

teaching.en: Sometimes I feel lost, but mistakes show me where the road turns.
teaching.es: A veces me siento perdido, pero los errores me muestran dónde gira el camino.
teaching.explanationEs: Sigues en el mismo campo: perdido, camino, giro. No cambies de imagen.
segments: Sometimes I feel lost, but mistakes
show me where the road turns.
teaching.audioText: Sometimes I feel lost, but mistakes show me where the road turns.

teaching.en: One day I will reach my destination and speak without a map.
teaching.es: Un día llegaré a mi destino y hablaré sin mapa.
teaching.explanationEs: El viaje termina en un destino: la metáfora se cierra con naturalidad.
segments: One day I will reach my
destination and speak without a map.
teaching.audioText: One day I will reach my destination and speak without a map.

teaching.en: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image becomes mixed.
teaching.es: Si el vocabulario es mi brújula pero la gramática es mi espada, la imagen queda mezclada.
teaching.explanationEs: Una espada no pertenece a un viaje: mezclar campos confunde al lector.
segments: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar
is my sword, the image becomes mixed.
teaching.audioText: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image becomes mixed.

teaching.en: Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed.
teaching.es: Mirando atrás, el viaje me enseñó que la paciencia importa más que la velocidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre reflexivo: Looking back + lección, dicha ya en sentido literal.
segments: Looking back, the journey taught me
that patience matters more than speed.
teaching.audioText: Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed.

prompt.es: Escribe el ensayo: una metáfora extendida sobre aprender un idioma y un cierre reflexivo.

answer.text: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning, I was at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a turn in the road that showed me a new way. Sometimes the road was long and sometimes I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.
accepted: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning, I was at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a turn in the road that showed me a new way. Sometimes the road was long and sometimes I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.

Learning English is a garden. On the first day I planted a few words, and every morning I watered them with a little practice. Some words grew quickly, and others needed more time, but I never stopped planting. Grammar was the ground, and my mistakes were the bad plants that I took out one by one. My teacher was a patient gardener, and my friends were the sun. Sometimes it was hard, and I felt lost in the garden. Looking back, the garden taught me that patience matters more than speed. Today I have a few flowers, and I am happy, but I will keep planting new words every day.

feedback.es: Un buen ensayo abre con la metáfora, la desarrolla con elementos del mismo campo sin mezclar imágenes y cierra con una reflexión literal.

origin.text: Escribe un ensayo de 110 a 160 palabras sobre aprender un idioma. Usa una sola metáfora extendida (por ejemplo, un viaje), al menos tres elementos de esa imagen y un cierre reflexivo (por ejemplo, con «Looking back»).
